questions.questionText: Where are sperm cells produced in the male reproductive system?
questions.hint: Think about the male gonads.
questions.explanation: The testes are the male gonads that produce sperm and testosterone.

questions.questionText: Where does fertilization normally occur in the female reproductive system?
questions.hint: Where does the egg travel after ovulation?
questions.explanation: Fertilization occurs in the Fallopian tube (oviduct).

questions.questionText: What is the function of the placenta during pregnancy?

options.text: Transports nutrients and oxygen to the fetus

questions.hint: Consider what the fetus needs from the mother's blood.
questions.explanation: The placenta allows exchange of gases, nutrients, and waste products between mother and fetus.

questions.questionText: How many chromosomes does a normal human somatic cell contain?
questions.hint: Think 23 pairs.
questions.explanation: Human somatic cells have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs).

questions.questionText: What is the main hormone that regulates the menstrual cycle?
questions.hint: Which female hormone is produced by the ovaries?
questions.explanation: Estrogen, produced by the ovaries, regulates the menstrual cycle.

questions.questionText: Which part of the sperm cell contains enzymes to penetrate the egg?
questions.hint: The tip of the sperm head contains digestive enzymes.
questions.explanation: The acrosome in the head of sperm contains enzymes to dissolve the egg's outer membrane.

questions.questionText: What is the average length of the menstrual cycle?
questions.hint: Think about a typical monthly cycle.
questions.explanation: The average menstrual cycle is 28 days, from day 1 of one period to day 1 of the next.

questions.questionText: During which phase of the menstrual cycle does ovulation occur?
questions.hint: Ovulation occurs around day 14 of a 28-day cycle.
questions.explanation: Ovulation occurs at the end of the follicular phase, around day 14.

questions.questionText: What is the function of luteinizing hormone (LH) in reproduction?
questions.hint: Which hormone causes the mature follicle to rupture?
questions.explanation: LH surge triggers ovulation, releasing the egg from the follicle.

questions.questionText: What happens to the corpus luteum if fertilization does not occur?

options.text: It degenerates into the corpus albicans
It becomes part of the placenta

questions.hint: Without pregnancy, the temporary endocrine structure breaks down.
questions.explanation: The corpus luteum degenerates into the corpus albicans if no pregnancy occurs.

questions.questionText: Which structure develops from the inner cell mass of the blastocyst?
questions.hint: The inner cell mass becomes the baby.
questions.explanation: The inner cell mass develops into the embryo (baby).

questions.questionText: What is the gestation period of a normal human pregnancy?
questions.hint: Count from conception to birth.
questions.explanation: Normal gestation is about 38 weeks from conception.

questions.questionText: What is the role of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)?
questions.hint: This hormone signals pregnancy to the body.
questions.explanation: hCG maintains the corpus luteum to continue producing progesterone early in pregnancy.

questions.questionText: Which week marks the end of the embryonic period in development?
questions.hint: When do major organs finish forming?
questions.explanation: The embryonic period ends at week 8 when all major organs are formed.

questions.questionText: During the follicular phase, rising levels of estrogen cause what effect on FSH?

options.text: FSH decreases due to negative feedback

questions.hint: Consider the feedback relationship between estrogen and FSH.
questions.explanation: Rising estrogen inhibits FSH secretion through negative feedback.

questions.questionText: What determines the sex of the offspring in humans?
questions.hint: Who carries the X or Y chromosome?
questions.explanation: The sperm carries either X or Y chromosome; the egg always carries X.

questions.questionText: In meiosis, what prevents Down syndrome in the offspring?

options.text: Nothing - errors can occur causing non-disjunction

questions.hint: Down syndrome is caused by an extra chromosome 21.
questions.explanation: Nothing actively prevents it; errors in meiosis (non-disjunction) can cause Down syndrome.

questions.questionText: The progesterone rise during the luteal phase causes what reproductive response?
questions.hint: Progesterone prepares the uterus for implantation.
questions.explanation: Progesterone maintains and thickens the uterine lining for potential implantation.

questions.questionText: What prevents polyspermy after one sperm enters the egg?
questions.hint: Multiple mechanisms prevent additional sperm entry.
questions.explanation: The slow block (depolarization) and cortical reaction prevent polyspermy.

questions.questionText: Which event in labor is triggered by oxytocin?
questions.hint: What hormone causes the uterus to contract during labor?
questions.explanation: Oxytocin stimulates powerful uterine contractions during labor and delivery.
